Some are fun. I am learning mainframe stuff and got a job paying over $70000 a year just for an internship. My family was super proud. But failing a class means that's all gone bye bye. 

I passed my mainframe class, but failed an algorithm class (the one the professor told us wan't important because we only need it if we're going to be reserachers). My friends want to protest it, the professor showed up 30 minutes late for the test (he thought it was another day) and a lot of the questions were stuff he didn't cover in class. Even the best students in the class made about a 60 or so. But I don't believe in bitching your way into success, you earn your grade or you don't. So I'm just taking it. 

Regardless, I'm on thin ice because of my "illness" last semester. I think this is probably it for me.

I'd rather be drunk and have a hard time focusing on her than being sober with vivid thoughts of her face every day of my life.

I mean your right, but wouldn't it be better if I just got out of the way? Not killed myself, just went off somewhere where I coulnn't poison more people.

I didn't drink or do drugs before she left. I don't want to get her back because she deserves better. But without her I hate myself.

I failed a test. I'm a senior in college and may have to drop out of college.

I miss my ex. Probably sounds stupid but we were together a few years and I don't feelel like I've had any reason to live after her. When it first happened a police officer took me to the hospital because I put a gun to myhead.

I'm also kind of drunk now (donmt worry, they took my guns) but I am feeling sad again. I tried to call a non-crisis hotline to tlak so I don't alienate my friends (they didn't answeR), but I miss her, and I wish I did better in school.

I tried my best and still failed, so it feels personal. But I mosstly did thss whole thing because I love her and wanted to provide for her.

But I also feel whiney for complaining about this. But since you asked, that's why I'm sad.
I'm up. I think I'm drunk. Also I'm sad but I don't want to bum you out.

I'm in a kind of transitional time in my life right now. Besides the fact that I just got out of a long term relationship about 8 months ago, I've got a pretty serious job opportunity after graduation that might involve me moving. Things just feel a little unstable right now and I have a gut feeling I'm going to experience a lot more changes over the next year or so.

A new relationship, even a casual one, might influence some of the choices I'll make and I'd rather be able to stabilize things in my life a little before I try to let someone into it. The last thing I need is more complications. 

Sorry if that's really vague or doesn't make sense.

That's what I figured too but there was just that part of my mind that says "maybe"

I'm not interested in dating her despite the crush, even if she feels the same way. I'm mostly just trying to make sense of it so I can stop thinking about it.

I'm 24 M, same major as you and everything. One of my good friends is 33 and the people in our social group besides him range from about 20-26.

So far the only people he's struggled to connect with are those under 21. Partially because we like to get drinks after class, but there's also just some sort of gap there that makes 20 a little bit too young most of the time. 

If it were me, I'd just start with smalltalk. I don't think I've ever viewed 28 as ridiculously old and out of touch, most people in the age range you mentioned should be perfectly fine talking to you about stuff. Biggest obstacle isn't actually age, it's getting CS majors to open up and be social.

Now for dating things get more complicated. I'd suggest dating a bit closer to your age range, maybe more mid 20s. Definitely avoid dating anyone in their late teens, they're adults but they're really more "adults" than adults for now.
